_comment: How the 1622 book is cut into four printed volumes.
`div` is the quod.lib.umich.edu 1:N number of the top-level division
(`tcp_to_typst.py --list` prints them).  `sections` is an inclusive range
of ORDINAL positions among that division's section divs -- position, not
the printed section number, because Gouge's numbering repeats itself and
two sections carry no number at all.  See section_divs() in
The volumes follow Gouge's own eight treatises: I; II-IV; V-VI; and
VII-VIII together with the part of Treatise I that expounds Ephesians
6:5-9, which belongs with them.  Chapters are an editorial division
within that -- Gouge wrote in numbered sections, not chapters -- and
every one of his section headings is kept underneath, so nothing of his

parallel-of-duties.title: A Parallel of the Duties of Husbands and Wives

volumes.subtitle: The First Treatise: An Exposition of That Part of Scripture Out of Which Domestical Duties Are Raised
volumes.back-lead: The first of Gouge's eight treatises: a verse-by-verse exposition of Ephesians 5:21-6:4, the passage the whole work is raised out of. Wives and husbands, children and parents, and above them the marriage of Christ and His church.

volumes.subtitle: The Second, Third and Fourth Treatises: Of Husband and Wife
volumes.back-lead: Who may marry and how a marriage is made; the duties husband and wife owe each other in common; and then, at length, the particular duties of wives and of husbands — each duty set against the fault that answers to it.

volumes.subtitle: The Fifth and Sixth Treatises: Of Children and Parents
volumes.back-lead: The duties children owe their parents — reverence, consent, obedience, and the recompense owed to age — and then the parents' own: love and prayer, nursing and nurture, teaching and correction, and the settling of a child in a calling and a marriage.

volumes.subtitle: The Seventh and Eighth Treatises: Of Servants and Masters
volumes.back-lead: The last of the eight treatises, with the exposition of Ephesians 6:5-9 they are raised out of: what a servant owes his master in reverence, obedience and faithfulness, and what a master owes his servants in authority, provision, employment and wages — under the Master they both have in heaven.
